chapter: On the road, James Brown and the 1956 crash
title: Therapy in the pool, a shorter leg and a built-up shoe
summary: After the cast, Cobb relearns movement, discovers the Hartford surgeons left his leg short, and gets a lift in his shoe made first in leather and then cork.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Yeah, well, I mean I had to go and -- and, you know, when they cut -- when Dr. Mayer cut that cast off me in the Hospital for Joint Disease, everything I had for muscle, all my skin just fell on the bed. I didn't have no muscle. And he sent a therapist up to me to take exercises. I had rotating exercises. He believed in that flexing. And she gave me that for two weeks before they put me down in the pool.

And the first day I went in the pool in the morning, they just let me dangle my legs. Then the next day the therapist got me and carried me to the table in the pool and gave me exercises. Then they picked me up and carried me

over and put me on the bar, and I rolled up on the bar and let my feet hang down, and that's when I found out that this leg was still and I had lost something on this side, and I couldn't touch with this foot, and I said -- and the therapist went down under the water and said, 'You about a inch and a half or three quarters short down there.' This was stiff. I couldn't even bend this leg or nothing (inaudible) from the time it was in the cast.

So I told Dr. Mayer about it. He told me to tell my doctors because I'm in the bed, and I'm spreaded out like this, and you can't tell until you bring them together, so he brought them together, and he could see the difference. But that was in Hartford where I'd lost an inch and three quarter bone right here. See that scar there? That's where it jumped out.

But they set it and didn't put a piece of bone in to make my leg the same length. So, he said, 'Only thing I can do is break it and add more, and he said, 'I'd rather not you go through this suffering anymore. We'll put a lift on your shoe, and if you want to do it later, then you do it, but I think you laid long enough now.'

So, he said, got a pair of shoes and sent it out, and he had built up for me because I'm getting ready to go. (inaudible). But they didn't do it in cork, they did it in leather, and that was a heavy shoe, and, oh, my God, I thought I was lifting a ton.
But I finally found out about the cork and all my shoes are done in cork now, and it's lighter.
